code defect vs semantics: the semantics text (exact integrality, Definition 8.6) is right. python/tvl/lints.py _check_float_precision's docstring defines precision-aligned as collision-free rounding, and for finite float sets the lint only checks collisions under round(v·P), so a non-aligned set such as {0.0001} at P=1000 gets no warning; its formal_property strings also cite 'Definition 8.5' (threshold rounding) instead of Definition 8.6. Options: A (recommended) make the lint check v·P ∈ ℤ for every value and cite Definition 8.6; B keep collision-only and relabel the warning as a collision check, not alignment. Text not edited.

code defect vs semantics: §9.5 says a point estimate outside the band is rejected; _test_banded_objective returns inconclusive when n < 2 before looking at the mean, so a one-observation (or aggregated n<2) bundle with an off-band mean is NoDecision, not Reject. Options: A (recommended) code: check the point estimate before the n<2 return (off-band → out_of_band), matching the semantics and spec §5.2 item 3; B semantics: add 'with at least two observations' to the rejection rule. Text not edited.
